authorization: User requested all 61 whole practice questions from Surface Area of Prisms and Cylinders; teaching content excluded.
method: Ordinary promotion in isolated staging, verified once and published through a checked transaction.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify familiar prisms from complete nets without measurements.

questions.mappingNote: All three nets preserve the source face connections and form the named rectangular or triangular prisms. Worked explanations follow the taught face-identification method.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify familiar prisms from complete nets without measurements.

classification.difficultyReason: Translate the open solid into five connected rectangles, matching wall dimensions to base edges and omitting the lid.

questions.mappingNote: The open box requires one 5 by 4 base, two 5 by 1 walls and two 4 by 1 walls. The solution net is accurate. Apply the diagram correction so interior floor edges do not show through the near walls.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Construct a dimensionally accurate net for an open rectangular box.

classification.difficultyReason: Construct valid nets by identifying matching end faces and arranging side rectangles; the triangular prism requires matching three different triangle edges to rectangle widths.

questions.mappingNote: Both solids preserve the source dimensions. The square-prism net has four 7 by 2 rectangles and two 2 by 2 squares. The triangular-prism net has congruent 3–4–5 ends and lateral rectangles of length 6. Both solution nets connect matching edges correctly.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Construct nets from the dimensions of a square prism and a triangular prism.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify solids from their face shapes and equality marks, mentally folding less familiar arrangements to distinguish their end faces.

questions.mappingNote: Identifying solids from their nets directly matches nets-of-prisms; cylinder recognition is included in this source exercise, with no cylinder-area calculation assessed.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify familiar solids from their faces and fold arrangements.

classification.difficultyReason: Add the supplied face areas on each prism net.

questions.mappingNote: Prompt, face-area givens, net connections and answers match the source. Independently verified 6×25=150 cm²; 2×147+2×126+2×42=630 mm²; and 3×280+2×75=990 m². All worked solutions correctly sum the faces using the taught method.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Add the supplied face areas on each prism net.

classification.difficultyReason: Use supplied nets and named face groups to select triangle or rectangle dimensions, calculate their areas and add; distinguish triangular height from sloping side length.

questions.mappingNote: The source teaching and scaffolds directly assess adding rectangular and triangular face areas to find prism surface area. Reading supplied nets supports that calculation rather than independently assessing net construction.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Rectangular prisms with paired nets and a scaffold for adding the areas of three pairs of faces.

classification.difficultyReason: Use given face areas and the equality of opposite faces to calculate total surface area.

questions.mappingNote: All face-area givens match the source. Verified paired areas 120, 96 and 40 m², giving 256 m²; cube totals are 2166 mm² and 253.5 m². Short and worked answers, taught methods and classification are correct.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Use given face areas and the equality of opposite faces to calculate total surface area.

classification.difficultyReason: Read the three dimensions and complete supplied paired-face multiplication and addition expressions; the full calculation structure is provided.

questions.mappingNote: The prompt, dimensions, face-pair scaffolds and answers match the source task. The three paired areas are 2×8×4=64 cm², 2×5×4=40 cm² and 2×8×5=80 cm², giving 184 cm². Worked solutions follow the taught method, and the Foundation classification and surface-area-prism mapping are appropriate.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Complete a supplied scaffold by calculating three pairs of rectangular faces and adding their areas.

classification.difficultyReason: Match dimensions to the explicitly named face pairs, double each rectangular area and add the results; decimal dimensions do not change the method.

questions.mappingNote: All dimensions and response headings match the source. Verified 42 + 60 + 140 = 242 cm² and 32.64 + 32.64 + 20.48 = 85.76 m². Both answer editions follow the taught face-pair method; classification is appropriate.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Calculate three pairs of rectangular face areas using supplied dimensions and scaffold labels.

classification.difficultyReason: Part (a) requires recognising that the equality marks establish only a square base, not a cube, and concluding that the unlabelled height prevents a numerical surface area. This assessment of insufficient information is the hardest demand; part (b) directly applies the taught face-pair method.

questions.mappingNote: surface-area-prism remains the closest skill: the source and supplied teaching assess rectangular face pairs and the dimensions needed to calculate their total area. No secondary skill is directly assessed; retain the existing rating.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Calculate surface area from solid diagrams using opposite pairs of rectangular faces.

classification.difficultyReason: Interpret outside painting of an open box as one base and four walls, then combine their rectangular areas without including a top.

questions.mappingNote: Prompt and dimensions match the source. Outside area is 17²+4(17×2.5)=459 cm², using the taught exposed-face method. Skill mapping is appropriate. Apply the diagram correction to hide interior base edges behind the two foreground walls.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Select the five outside faces of an open box and exclude the missing top.

classification.difficultyReason: Explain why adding individual surface areas counts internal contact faces, identifying two hidden faces at each of the two joins.

questions.mappingNote: Prompt, dimensions and three-layer comparison match the source. Two joins conceal four 12×9 faces. Independently, one prism has area 321 cm² and the stack has area 531 cm², versus 963 cm² for three separate prisms. Both explanations correctly repair the source’s two-face statement. Composite-solid classification is appropriate.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Explain why joining identical prisms reduces their total exposed surface area.

classification.difficultyReason: Model each covered book as a rectangular prism, scale its surface area to 1000 books and convert square centimetres to square metres using the squared length conversion.

questions.mappingNote: The task directly assesses prism surface area in context. The supplied skill list has no specific area-unit conversion skill to add as a secondary mapping.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Calculate a rectangular prism’s surface area, scale to 1000 books and convert square centimetres to square metres.

classification.difficultyReason: Derive a general expression and factorise it to obtain the rectangular-prism formula.

questions.mappingNote: Prompt, symbolic dimensions and both parts match the source. Two faces of each area give SA=2lb+2lh+2bh; factorising gives 2(lb+lh+bh). Worked answers follow the taught face-pair method. surface-area-prism is the closest supplied skill.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Derive a general expression and factorise it to obtain the rectangular-prism formula.

classification.difficultyReason: Read the three dimensions from each prism and substitute them into the supplied surface-area formula. All dimensions use consistent units, so no conversion or additional geometric inference is required.

questions.mappingNote: All dimensions and units match the source. Independently calculated 2(360+810+900)=4140 cm², 2(3120+2275+1680)=14150 mm² and 2(39+17.68+25.5)=164.36 m². Short and worked answers are correct, use the derived formula and require no rounding instruction. Skill mapping is appropriate.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: The source places these formula-substitution questions in Mastery; dimensions include decimals and several units.

classification.difficultyReason: Express one square face area as s squared and generalise to six equal faces to form the surface-area formula.

questions.mappingNote: Six square faces each have area s², giving SA=6s². The diagram preserves three side-length labels and correct cube connectivity.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Generalise surface area to a cube using a symbolic side length.

classification.difficultyReason: Find the area of three pairs of faces, then round the required number of paint tins up to a whole number and calculate the cost.

questions.mappingNote: Surface area is 2(0.8+1.2+1.5)=7 m². Coverage requires 1.75 tins, so two whole tins cost $16. The worked solution follows the taught paired-face method.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Find the area of three pairs of faces, then round the required number of paint tins up to a whole number and calculate the cost.

classification.difficultyReason: Form surface-area equations from labelled dimensions; the hardest part multiplies algebraic lengths, collects squared terms and selects the positive square root for a length.

questions.mappingNote: Retain surface-area-prism: the source asks for missing rectangular-prism dimensions using surface-area equations. Label changes do not alter the accepted mapping.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Form and solve surface-area equations for missing dimensions, including dimensions expressed as multiples of the same unknown.

classification.difficultyReason: Find an unknown cube side length from its surface area using six equal square faces.

questions.mappingNote: Six equal square faces give 150=6x², so the positive side length is 5 m. Prompt, answer and working match the source and taught method.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Find an unknown cube side length from its surface area using six equal square faces.

classification.difficultyReason: Expresses surface areas in terms of a shared side length and simplifies their ratio.

questions.mappingNote: Prompt, dimensions, midpoint cut and both answers match the source. The worked solution correctly compares the original prism with one cube, using paired face areas. Skill mapping is appropriate.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Expresses surface areas in terms of a shared side length and simplifies their ratio.

classification.difficultyReason: Uses a volume and a dimension ratio to determine lengths before calculating surface area.

questions.mappingNote: Prompt and both parts match the source. Positive side lengths follow from x³=8; the resulting surface area is 184 cm². Expanded working preserves the source method and the surface-area teaching. Skill mapping is appropriate.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Uses a volume and a dimension ratio to determine lengths before calculating surface area.

classification.difficultyReason: Use equal-edge marks and the common prism length to infer equal rectangular face areas, then count two triangular ends and three rectangles.

questions.mappingNote: Face areas and equal-edge marks match the source. Independently calculated 2×76+3×82=398 mm² and 2×24+3×44=180 cm². Worked answers and skill mapping are correct.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Add supplied face areas, using equal-edge marks to identify three equal rectangular faces.

classification.difficultyReason: For the unscaffolded prisms, identify the perpendicular triangle sides despite changed orientation, calculate both ends and all three rectangular faces, then add.

questions.mappingNote: Retain surface-area-prism: the source and teaching sum triangular ends and rectangular faces. The changes introduce no additional assessed skill.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Add the areas of triangular ends and rectangular faces using supplied dimensions and scaffolds.

classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish the triangle's perpendicular height from its unequal sloping sides, using the height for end areas and all three side lengths for rectangular faces.

questions.mappingNote: The prompt, five measurements, triangular altitude, short answer and worked answer match the source. The triangle is consistent: the 8 mm altitude gives base segments 6 mm and 15 mm from sides 10 mm and 17 mm, totaling 21 mm. All five face areas and their sum are correct; no rounding is needed.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: The source Foundation question supplies all dimensions needed to calculate the five face areas.

classification.difficultyReason: Link Pythagoras to face-area calculations, distinguishing missing legs from hypotenuses. The hardest part requires identifying an undrawn altitude in an isosceles end; halving the base is explicitly prompted.

questions.mappingNote: Surface-area-prism is the closest supplied skill and matches the source's explicit Pythagoras-then-surface-area task. Pythagoras is directly assessed, but no standalone Pythagoras skill record is supplied for secondary selection; unrelated skills are unnecessary.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Use Pythagoras’ Theorem to obtain a missing cross-section measurement before summing the areas of the two triangles and three rectangles.

classification.difficultyReason: Interpret differently oriented prisms, find missing triangle dimensions using Pythagoras, and assemble all face areas. The equilateral end requires constructing an altitude and halving its base without a drawn guide.

questions.mappingNote: All four prompts, dimensions, equality and right-angle marks match the source. Pythagorean calculations, face areas, totals and rounding are correct.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Find missing cross-section lengths using Pythagoras’ theorem before calculating the areas of the prism’s faces.

classification.difficultyReason: Translate the triangular ends and three rectangular faces into a surface-area equation, then subtract the fixed end areas and solve for the common prism length.

questions.mappingNote: The diagram preserves the source dimensions and unknown prism length. The two triangular ends total 24 cm² and the rectangles total 18x cm², giving x = 11 cm. Both answers and the source worked equation are correct.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Form and solve a linear equation from the triangular and rectangular face areas.

classification.difficultyReason: Match the cylinder height and circumference to the supplied net, then calculate its explicitly separated circular and rectangular areas and add them.

questions.mappingNote: Directly develops closed-cylinder surface area through the taught net decomposition. Existing rating and mapping remain valid.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify net dimensions, calculate its component areas and add them using the taught closed-cylinder method.

classification.difficultyReason: Read radius and height from each diagram and substitute into the taught cylinder formula. Later parts require recognising a supplied diameter and halving it before substitution.

questions.mappingNote: All parts directly apply closed-cylinder surface area, including radius identification from diameter. Existing rating and mapping remain valid.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Apply the taught closed-cylinder formula, distinguishing given radii from diameters and rounding to one decimal place.

classification.difficultyReason: Apply the closed-cylinder formula, distinguish radius from diameter, and retain exact multiples of pi.

questions.mappingNote: All six diagrams preserve the source dimensions and radius/diameter distinctions. Independently calculated surface areas are respectively 8π m², 14π cm², 192π cm², 16π m², 150π cm² and 36π m². Short and worked answers agree and use the taught method.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Apply the closed-cylinder formula, distinguish radius from diameter, and retain exact multiples of pi.

classification.difficultyReason: Calculate and compare two closed-cylinder surface areas, then justify the comparison.

questions.mappingNote: Source radii and heights are preserved. A has surface area 2π(5²)+2π(5)(3)=80π cm²; B has 2π(3²)+2π(3)(5)=48π cm². Both answers correctly justify that A is larger.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Calculate and compare two closed-cylinder surface areas, then justify the comparison.

classification.difficultyReason: Increase the height by 10%, recalculate total surface area with unchanged circular ends, then express the area difference as a percentage of the original total.

questions.mappingNote: Original surface area is 768π cm², rounding to 2412.7 cm². Increasing height to 22 cm gives 816π cm², rounding to 2563.5 cm². Using exact areas gives a percentage increase of (48/768)×100%=6.25%. Prompts, answers and worked methods are correct.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Apply the closed-cylinder formula, increase the height by a percentage, and compare the resulting surface areas.

classification.difficultyReason: Calculate curved and total surface areas, then express their ratio as a percentage.

questions.mappingNote: Radius 2.2 cm and height 8.5 cm match the source. Curved area is 37.4π cm², total area is 47.08π cm², and their percentage is 79.44%. Exact arithmetic before final rounding follows the teaching. Cylinder surface area is the closest skill.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Calculate curved and total surface areas, then express their ratio as a percentage.

classification.difficultyReason: The hardest parts reverse circumference or area formulas to obtain a radius, then use it in a different formula; the shaded-region task additionally selects one quarter of the circle.

questions.mappingNote: All four prompts and givens match the source. Independently obtained a: 36π cm²; b: 192π cm² using radius 6 cm; c: 49π/16 cm² using radius 3.5 cm and a quarter-area; d: 8π cm ≈ 25.13 cm using radius 4 cm. Worked methods are appropriate. Cylinder surface area is the closest available group mapping, with part b directly assessing it.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Uses circle measurements, exact answers and reverse calculations supporting the closed-cylinder formula.

classification.difficultyReason: Rearrange the curved-surface-area formula to find an unknown height.

questions.mappingNote: The source givens yield h = 754/(12π) ≈ 20.00047 cm, correctly reported as 20.00 cm to the added two-decimal-place instruction. Rearranging the taught curved-area expression is appropriate, and the skill mapping fits.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Rearrange the curved-surface-area formula to find an unknown height.

classification.difficultyReason: Substitute the radius into the closed-cylinder formula and solve for height using exact multiples of π.

questions.mappingNote: The source givens yield 32π + 8πh = 128π, hence h = 12 m exactly. Both answers, the taught closed-cylinder method and the skill mapping are correct.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Substitute the radius into the closed-cylinder formula and solve for height using exact multiples of π.

classification.difficultyReason: Substitute algebraic radius and height into the closed-cylinder formula and solve for a positive length.

questions.mappingNote: Source radius x and height 5x are correctly represented. Substitution gives 12πx²=972π and positive length x=9. Both answers and the cylinder skill mapping are correct.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Substitute algebraic radius and height into the closed-cylinder formula and solve for a positive length.

classification.difficultyReason: Equate the surface areas of two different solids and solve for the cube's edge length.

questions.mappingNote: Source cylinder radius 5 cm, height 9 cm and cube edge x are preserved. Cylinder area is 140π cm²; equating this to 6x² gives x=8.56 cm to 2 d.p. Worked method and cylinder/prism mappings are appropriate.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Equate the surface areas of two different solids and solve for the cube's edge length.

classification.difficultyReason: Explain how changing the height affects the curved surface and circular ends separately.

questions.mappingNote: Prompt and explanation match the source. With radius unchanged, doubling height doubles 2πrh while 2πr² remains unchanged, so total surface area is not doubled.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Explain how changing the height affects the curved surface and circular ends separately.

classification.difficultyReason: Derives a radius from circular face area, connects area and volume, and applies the closed-cylinder surface-area formula.

questions.mappingNote: The diagram correctly gives circular face area 18 cm² and height 9 cm. All four independently derived answers are correct. Part d clearly refers to the original cylinder and explicitly states the rounding required by the source answer. The cylinder surface-area mapping fits the most advanced assessed task.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Derives a radius from circular face area, connects area and volume, and applies the closed-cylinder surface-area formula.

classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the highlighted axial triangle, use Pythagoras to find a diameter, halve it for the radius, and substitute into cylinder surface area while retaining precision.

questions.mappingNote: Prompt, dimensions, Pythagoras calculations, radii, surface areas, rounding and skill mapping are correct after the diagram correction.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Each part requires Pythagoras’ theorem to recover the diameter before applying the closed-cylinder surface-area formula.

classification.difficultyReason: Infer the can dimensions from tight sphere packing, distinguish two material costs, convert area units and calculate a production cost.

questions.mappingNote: Packing gives r = 37 mm and h = 222 mm. Areas, square-unit conversions, 16000 cans, material rates and final cost are correct. The worked solution follows the taught separation of circular ends and curved surface.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Infer the can dimensions from tight sphere packing, distinguish two material costs, convert area units and calculate a production cost.

classification.difficultyReason: Choose which end faces, curved portions and cut rectangles remain for each stated opening. The closed quarter-cylinder requires combining two quarter-circle ends, quarter curved area and two full cut rectangles.

questions.mappingNote: All answers and classification are correct once the diagram corrections are applied. Independently obtained 431.25π, 2.3625π, 8.4π+12.88, 288π, 5.555π, 399π, 48π+120, 2.24π and 16.25π+20 in the respective square units.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify exposed curved, circular and rectangular surfaces from supplied dimensions.

classification.difficultyReason: Translate snug packing into a cylinder radius and shared box length, calculate both closed-box surface areas, and subtract to interpret the cardboard saving.

questions.mappingNote: Closed square-prism packaging has area 352 cm²; cylindrical packaging has area 88π cm². The saving rounds to 76 cm². The source display flap is compatible with the explicit closed-box comparison. Teaching and skill mappings are appropriate.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Compare the surface areas of two closed packages with different cross-sections.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify the exposed curved half-cylinder surface, convert diameter to radius and round the area to the nearest square metre.

questions.mappingNote: Prompt and diagram preserve the open-ended shelter, diameter 3.8 m and length 10 m. Only the curved roof contributes: (1/2)(2π)(1.9)(10)=19π≈59.6903 m², giving 60 m². Both answers use the taught component method. The partial-cylinder skill is appropriate.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify the exposed curved half-cylinder surface, convert diameter to radius and round the area to the nearest square metre.

classification.difficultyReason: Build separate surface-area totals for triangular and semicircular prism tents, including both ends and floors, then compare and calculate the difference. Required triangle dimensions are supplied.

questions.mappingNote: Both diagrams preserve the source dimensions and meaningful marks. Using the supplied rounded sloping length 2.24 m, the triangular tent area is 2(1/2×2×2)+2(2.24×5)+2×5=36.4 m². The half-cylinder tent area is π+5π+10=10+6π≈28.8496 m². The difference is approximately 7.5504 m², rounding to 7.6 m². Both ends and floors are included, and the worked method and primary/secondary skill mappings are appropriate.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Compare two different solids by including their end faces, curved or sloping surfaces and rectangular floors.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify the exposed inside surfaces of an open cylinder, calculate paint coverage, and round the number of cans up.

questions.mappingNote: Prompt and diagram preserve height 1.5 m, diameter 6 m, the open top and the required inside floor. With radius 3 m, painted area is 2π(3)(1.5)+π(3)²=18π m². Paint required is 18π/9=2π litres, so 7 one-litre cans are needed. Exact arithmetic is retained before rounding, and the partial-cylinder skill is appropriate.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify the exposed inside surfaces of an open cylinder, calculate paint coverage, and round the number of cans up.

classification.difficultyReason: Separate the floor from the canvas surfaces of a half-cylinder and apply different material rates.

questions.mappingNote: Source prompt and dimensions are preserved. Floor area is 27.3 m²; canvas area is 18.06π m²; cost is $1696.53 to two decimal places, hence $1697. Working follows the taught surface-by-surface method.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Separate the floor from the canvas surfaces of a half-cylinder and apply different material rates.

classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish retained sector angles from removed wedges, scale both end areas and curved area by the retained fraction, and add two unscaled cut rectangles. The arc-length hint supplies the curved-surface route.

questions.mappingNote: Source prompts, angles, radii, heights, exact answers and classification are correct. Independently derived totals are (60π+48) m², (800π/3+1600) cm², (135π/2+36) cm² and (70π/3+12) cm². Apply the diagram corrections to make the exposed radial faces and rear edges geometrically consistent.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Calculate exact surface areas of sector cylinders, interpreting retained and removed angles and including both radial cut faces.

classification.difficultyReason: Match diagram dimensions to the supplied face-area expressions and evaluate them; the scaffolding supplies the face grouping, formulas and multiplicities.

questions.mappingNote: These are single prisms with parallelogram, trapezoidal and rhombic cross-sections; prism surface area is the closest supplied skill. Existing rating remains valid.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Face-area scaffolds support direct substitution using supplied measurements.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify matching end faces and side rectangles, distinguish perpendicular heights from sloping edges, and convert mixed lengths to consistent units before summing areas.

questions.mappingNote: Each task assesses summing the faces of one prism. Unit conversion supports that calculation; no additional supplied skill is directly assessed. Existing rating and mapping remain valid.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Students identify and sum every face without a supplied scaffold; part g also requires unit conversion.

classification.difficultyReason: Interpret equal-edge marks, subtract the wall height from the total height, split the tent ends into rectangles and triangles, and convert the complete canvas area into cost.

questions.mappingNote: Equal-edge marks supply 1.5 m wall and roof lengths; triangular height is 1.3 m. Total area is 21.45 m² and canvas costs $107.25. Remove the incorrectly exposed rear-left roof edges as corrected below.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Interpret equal-edge marks, split the pentagonal ends into rectangles and triangles, then calculate canvas cost.

classification.difficultyReason: Combine triangular and semicircular end areas with exposed flat and curved lateral surfaces, excluding the internal join.

questions.mappingNote: The diameter is 5 cm, so r = 2.5 cm. Exposed surface area is 2(6 + 3.125π) + 36 + 27 + 22.5π = 75 + 28.75π = 165.32 cm². The internal rectangular join is correctly excluded. Composite-solids primary and partial-cylinder secondary mappings fit.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Combine triangular and semicircular end areas with exposed flat and curved lateral surfaces, excluding the internal join.

classification.difficultyReason: Construct the relevant right triangle, including a height difference in part a, use the explicitly requested Pythagoras procedure, then use the missing length in the face-area sum.

questions.mappingNote: Part (a): x = √(15² + 8²) = 17 cm; area = 450 + 399 + 231 + 357 + 315 = 1752 cm². Part (b): x = √(53² − 45²) = 28 mm; area = 9800 + 12190 + 40250 = 62240 mm². Both preserve source givens and use face-by-face prism calculations; the prism skill mapping fits.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Use Pythagoras’ Theorem to find a missing cross-section length before calculating and summing face areas.

classification.difficultyReason: Determine composite cross-sectional areas and complete exposed perimeters for the supplied formula, excluding internal joins while including curved boundaries and both radial cut edges of the three-quarter circle.

questions.mappingNote: Source content, givens, formula annotations, answers, worked methods and classification are correct after the part f diagram correction.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Apply a general prism formula to composite, concave and curved cross-sections, including newly exposed cut faces.

classification.difficultyReason: Calculate the roof height from two given heights, then combine the areas of all exposed faces.

questions.mappingNote: All source dimensions and construction marks are retained. Roof height is 11−8=3 cm; the two pentagonal ends contribute 152 cm² and the longitudinal faces contribute 272 cm², giving 424 cm². Worked decomposition and composite-solids mapping are correct.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Calculate the roof height from two given heights, then combine the areas of all exposed faces.

classification.difficultyReason: Reinterpret one sixth of the regular hexagonal cross-section as an equilateral triangle, infer its height from half the full hexagon height, and include the newly exposed rectangular cut faces.

questions.mappingNote: The regular hexagon divides into six equilateral triangular cross-sections. Using the supplied height, each triangle has altitude 5.2 cm. Two triangular ends contribute 31.2 cm² and three rectangular faces contribute 180 cm², giving 211.2 cm² to one decimal place. Source content, working and prism mapping are correct.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify the equilateral triangular cross-section produced by the cuts, halve the supplied across-flats height, and count all five exposed faces of each triangular prism.

classification.difficultyReason: Work backwards from cube surface area to its side length, interpret the enclosed cylinder's height and diameter as that length, then calculate its closed surface area.

questions.mappingNote: The cube side is √(216÷6)=6 cm, so the inscribed cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 6 cm. Its closed surface area is 54π≈169.65 cm². Source content, rounding, working and cylinder mapping are correct.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Infer the cylinder's radius and height from the surface area of its enclosing cube before applying the closed-cylinder formula.

classification.difficultyReason: Calculate two square areas and their difference, then substitute into the supplied exposed-face expression; the scaffolding already determines which surfaces to count.

questions.mappingNote: Joined cubes require excluding their contact surfaces, directly assessing composite-solid surface area. Existing rating and mapping remain valid.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: The labelled faces and supplied scaffold guide the calculation of exposed areas.

classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish joined surfaces from exposed surfaces across several solids; the hardest parts require interpreting through-holes as adding interior walls while removing end regions, or deriving a sloping edge before excluding the joined footprint.

questions.mappingNote: Independent results: (a) 46π ≈ 144.5 cm²; (b) 1028 cm²; (c) 600 + 80π ≈ 851.3 m²; (d) 35500 + 40√14225 ≈ 40270.7 cm²; (e) 3400π + 3350 ≈ 14031.4 cm²; (f) 45160 cm². Worked solutions correctly sum exposed surfaces or subtract both joined faces, consistent with the supplied teaching context.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Combine familiar surface areas, exclude joined faces and derive one sloping length.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert the length to centimetres and diameters to radii, then combine two annular ends with inner and outer curved surfaces, all explicitly requested in the task.

questions.mappingNote: Correct after the diagram correction. Both diameters, the length conversion, annular ends and internal and external curved surfaces are represented correctly. The composite-solids classification is appropriate.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert metres to centimetres and combine annular ends with internal and external curved surfaces.

questions.note: The changed TikZ preserves single equality marks on AB and BF, matching the source's two equal base edges. No height equality or dimension is introduced, so the accepted insufficient-information answer remains valid. Other edges, dimensions and answers are unchanged.

bankProjection.note: Source-confirmed category headings are omitted only from bank prompts and presentation. Explicit equivalent fraction notation repairs satisfy bank validation. Source booklet content and all questions are retained.
